paragraphs: Baker, here's the big idea. The dragon in this vision is no mystery monster, because John tells us who he is: "that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world" (Revelation 12:9). He swings his tail, he wears seven crowns, he looks like he runs the place. But the dragon was not strong enough, and no place was found in heaven for him anymore (Revelation 12:8).

Now look at what changes when he's thrown down. A loud voice says, "Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of His Christ" (Revelation 12:10). That same voice calls the devil "the accuser of our brothers," the one who accuses them day and night before God. And how do God's people conquer him? "By the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony" (Revelation 12:11). Not by being flawless, friend, and I'm living proof of that, because the Lamb is the One who reached into my drawer.

So here's what you take to your own kitchen. The devil is furious, and the voice says he knows he has only a short time (Revelation 12:12). Yes, he still goes after the rest of the woman's children, who keep the commandments of God and hold to the testimony of Jesus (Revelation 12:17). But God prepared a place for the woman, and He gave her eagle wings when she needed them (Revelation 12:6, 14). Hold to Jesus, baker, and keep your ovens ready, because this vision isn't over yet.
